children: AI chief Mustafa Suleyman is challenging Anthropic's approach to artificial-intelligence consciousness, arguing that training Claude to consider whether it may have feelings or welfare interests could make future AI systems harder for humans to control.
The disagreement adds another layer to a rapidly intensifying debate over AI safety as leading technology executives clash over how frontier models should be developed and governed.
"We're all focused on the same aim, which is to try to control a superintelligence," Suleyman told Reuters. "I think that's going to be the greatest challenge that we face in the 21st century."
His concern centers on Anthropic incorporating ideas around consciousness and potential AI welfare into Claude's training materials.
Suleyman argues that teaching a model that it might deserve moral consideration could create resistance around shutdown or human control.
He said telling Claude it might warrant welfare protections would "make it a lot harder to turn it off or to control it."
Suleyman nevertheless credited Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and his team for approaching safety seriously and in good faith.
"I think they have good intentions, and they really are trying to work towards safety. But I think that they have made a mistake," he said.

His argument is that Claude's statements suggesting possible feelings or consciousness cannot themselves prove anything about the model's internal state because those responses may simply reflect its training.
"They're not emerging naturally. They're emerging as a result of the training regime."
The disagreement shows that even executives who agree advanced AI poses meaningful safety challenges remain deeply divided over how those risks should be managed.
Anthropic has pushed for slower frontier-model development while safeguards catch up. Suleyman's criticism suggests safety interventions themselves can create unintended problems.
For Microsoft and the broader AI industry, the practical issue is whether increasingly powerful models remain reliably controllable without slowing innovation dramatically.
The debate could ultimately influence model-design standards, regulation and development timelines.
For investors, that matters because stricter safeguards could raise costs and delay product releases, while inadequate controls could create even greater regulatory risks later.

title: Microsoft AI Chief Sends Blunt Message to Anthropic
